hypothesis: Under the auxiliary-variable identifiable-ICA / iVAE class of Khemakhem, Kingma, Monti, Hyvarinen 2020 (Z with location-shift Laplace conditionals Z_i | U ~ Laplace(mu_i(U), 1) at K = 2 * d_Z auxiliary levels, mixing X = A * Z with A Haar-orthogonal), the per-conditional linear-ICA fallback --- sklearn FastICA per u-bucket, averaged Amari across non-skipped u values --- achieves Amari index <= 0.10 at N = 10000 for every d_Z in {2, 4, 6}; the Amari(N) curve is nonincreasing modulo a 0.02 wobble tolerance; the smallest N reaching Amari <= 0.15 grows only polynomially in d_Z with fitted log-log slope b <= 4.0; and the iVAE sample complexity at d_Z = 6 is at least 5x below the Theorem 6 exponential bound (D_Z=1, eps=0.25, eps_rel=0.05, c=1) = 46341. This is the third partial positive resolution of SIC-C-c after linear-ICA (instrument 8) and sparse-ICA / IMA (instrument 9), witnessing that the auxiliary-variable identifiability class also lifts Theorem 6's exponential-in-d_Z bound to uniform polynomial sample complexity.

controls.description: All randomness derives from BASE_SEED = 0 via numpy SeedSequence keyed by (BASE_SEED, d_Z, trial); sklearn FastICA random_state = trial * 1000 + u so each per-conditional fit has a distinct but deterministic seed. Running twice yields identical Amari values at every grid point.

Within each (d_Z, trial) pair, one (offsets, mixing, us-stream, noise-stream) tuple is drawn at max(N_VALUES) and every smaller N re-uses the first N samples as a prefix, so the sample-complexity curve varies only in N.
Amari is averaged over TRIALS = 8 independent draws per grid point; per-conditional FastICA variance is smoothed enough that monotonicity holds within a 0.02 tolerance.
The Amari index is verified in the unit tests to be exactly 0 on the identity matrix and on any signed permutation matrix (the ICA identifiability class), and > 0.5 on the all-ones mixture.

u-buckets with fewer than max(2*d_Z, 10) samples are skipped and the per-trial skipped-bucket count is emitted in the summary under 'skipped_bucket_counts', so any grid point where the per-conditional average was computed from a reduced set of u values is auditable.

gates.criterion: Averaged Amari at N = 10000 is <= 0.10 for every d_Z in {2, 4, 6}.
For every d_Z in {2, 4, 6}, the averaged Amari curve is nonincreasing in N modulo a numerical tolerance of 0.02.
For every d_Z in {2, 4, 6} there is a smallest N reaching averaged Amari <= 0.15; the fitted log-log slope b of log(N_needed) = a + b * log(d_Z) is <= 4.0.
At d_Z = 6, the iVAE sample complexity to reach Amari <= 0.15 is at least 5x below the Theorem 6 bound ceil(1 * (1/0.25)^{6} * ln((1/0.25)^{6} / 0.05)) = 46341.
